description: STORM OS gaming defaults (applied with -EnableGamingDefaults). Documented per-user Windows gaming settings; no power, driver, service, security or network changes. Every value can be changed back in Settings.

settings.name: Game Mode on
settings.description: Windows Game Mode prioritizes the game and pauses Windows Update driver installs and restart notifications while playing.
settings.reason: More consistent frame times; Game Mode is Microsoft's supported mechanism for this.

settings.name: Optimizations for windowed games
settings.description: DirectX 10/11 games in windowed or borderless mode use the flip presentation model.
settings.reason: Lower latency and better frame pacing in borderless windowed games, with support for VRR.
settings.userChange: Settings > System > Display > Graphics > Advanced graphics settings > Optimizations for windowed games

settings.name: Background recording off
settings.description: Game Bar does not continuously record gameplay in the background ("Record what happened"). Manual captures still work.
settings.reason: Avoids constant GPU encoder and disk load while playing.
settings.userChange: Settings > Gaming > Captures > Record what happened

settings.name: Enhance pointer precision off
settings.description: Mouse movement is not accelerated: the cursor moves proportionally to the mouse.
settings.reason: Consistent, predictable aim in games; common default for gaming mice.
settings.userChange: Settings > Bluetooth & devices > Mouse > Additional mouse settings > Pointer Options > Enhance pointer precision

settings.name: Pointer acceleration threshold 1
settings.description: First acceleration threshold used together with Enhance pointer precision.
settings.reason: Part of turning off pointer acceleration (Windows sets all three values together).
settings.userChange: Settings > Bluetooth & devices > Mouse > Additional mouse settings > Pointer Options > Enhance pointer precision

settings.name: Pointer acceleration threshold 2
settings.description: Second acceleration threshold used together with Enhance pointer precision.
settings.reason: Part of turning off pointer acceleration (Windows sets all three values together).
settings.userChange: Settings > Bluetooth & devices > Mouse > Additional mouse settings > Pointer Options > Enhance pointer precision
